clue.text: Wise fool ignoring content of inane books

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

indicators.note: ignoring the contents of the word inane keeps just its outside letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, the usual crossword books

explanation.surface: A wise person is a fool for skipping the substance of silly books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring content of' leaves IE, the outer letters of 'inane'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal synonym for wise or discerning.

clue.text: Not so dense, spelling "bum" right

parts.note: arse is British slang for bottom, the same as bum

explanation.surface: Someone a bit less stupid now spells the word bum correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' is British slang for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparser means more thinly scattered, the comparative opposite of denser.

clue.text: Dotty pants a lot after giving birth

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so these letters go haywire

explanation.surface: A dotty person panting a lot just after labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period following childbirth, used here adjectivally like the phrase.

clue.text: Jet set romps regularly in bar

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase Jet set romps

explanation.surface: Rich partygoers frolic frequently in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the legal verb, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Travelling to the pole, in need of pap

indicators.note: travelling means moving around, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Heading to the North Pole requires soft baby food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pap' looks like mushy food; it is short for paparazzo, a celebrity photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paparazzi need long-range lenses to snap celebrities from a distance.

clue.text: Will supplement of fish oil initially improve capacity for love?

parts.note: cod is a common fish

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, taking its place in the word oil

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of improve and capacity

explanation.surface: Could cod-liver oil boost a person's ability to love?
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives IC, the first letters of 'improve capacity', which replace O ('love') in OIL to make ICIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is an addition or amendment appended to a will.

clue.text: Provide grub, but not support

indicators.note: but not means excluding the following word's letters

parts.note: a grub is a larva, such as a caterpillar
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: Supply food, though not any backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide grub' also reads as the full definition, since to cater is to supply food.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply what is needed, especially food for an event.

clue.text: A country boy turned up to welcome American Buddhist

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in a newcomer
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mali is an African country
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rural youngster flipped up to greet an American Buddhist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses A MALI LAD to DALILAMA, then 'to welcome' admits A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Charlie grew old behind bars

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: Charlie got old while in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Caged means confined in an enclosure of bars, like an imprisoned animal.

clue.text: Cordial setter's absorbed in short newspaper article

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside the next piece
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article
the setter refers to themself, so setter's becomes I'm

explanation.surface: A friendly puzzle-maker engrossed in a brief editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective meaning warm; it is the drink. 'setter's' is the crossword convention for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit-flavoured drink, as is a lime-based soft drink.

clue.text: Mates saunter about surrounding bit of property

indicators.note: about signals that the concealed letters are read backwards
the words Mates saunter surround the letters wanted, which run across them

explanation.surface: Friends stroll around a piece of land they own.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is an item of value someone owns, so one piece of their property.

clue.text: Leaves Gillette founders with millions

indicators.note: founders as a verb means collapses or sinks, so the word Gillette breaks up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: The people who founded the razor company Gillette became millionaires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founders' looks like a noun about the company's creators; it is the verb 'collapses', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Gem is a small lettuce variety, and lettuce is eaten as salad leaves.

clue.text: Abrasive doctor appears extremely narked

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
extremely takes the extreme letters of narked, its first and last

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered doctor looks very irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician in the scene; it is the verb meaning tamper with, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is an abrasive material used for smoothing surfaces, here used as a noun.

clue.text: Find FIFA banning all females in Asian country

indicators.note: banning means excluding the named letters from the phrase Find FIFA

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, and all of them means every F

explanation.surface: Discover that football's governing body excludes women.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing all three Fs from FINDFIFA leaves the country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Are sick of blighter with shed

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a blighter is a contemptible person, a wretch

explanation.surface: Fed up with a scoundrel who has a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut; it is the verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave or vomit, a plural-verb match for be sick.

clue.text: Help the French ban kind of moustache

parts.note: to give a hand is to help
le is French for the
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Assist the French in banning a certain style of facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A handlebar moustache is a long, curled style shaped like bicycle bars.

clue.text: Institution raising issue of defunct generators

definitions.text: Institution raising issue of defunct generators

parts.words: Institution raising issue of defunct generators
parts.note: issue means offspring and generators are parents, so this is a home bringing up children whose parents have died, disguised as industry talk

explanation.surface: Sounds like a body flagging up a problem with obsolete power generators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children and 'generators' those who begat them.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution caring for children who have lost their parents is a home for orphans.

clue.text: Say obscene words about substandard game

parts.note: read as sub standard: par is the standard, and the next piece goes beneath it

indicators.note: about means the pieces turn round

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
dirt is smutty talk

explanation.surface: Swear about some second-rate sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substandard' splits into 'sub standard': in this down entry the reversed EG DIRT sits under PAR. 'about' turns EGDIRT into TRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird shot for sport and eaten.

clue.text: Write on sex with variable confidence

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to author a text is to write it
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Pen something about sex with shifting assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with authority means speaking with confident command of a subject.

clue.text: Half-hearted hostility and dismal dazzle

indicators.note: half-hearted means losing half of the doubled letter at the heart of the word

parts.note: spleen is bad temper or hostility
dour means gloomy or dismal

explanation.surface: Lukewarm animosity combined with gloom makes a strange kind of brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two central Es of SPLEEN, giving SPLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or brilliance, the quality that dazzles, both nouns.

clue.text: Half-inch fairy kindles revolt

indicators.note: revolt means turning over, so the pieces go upside down

parts.note: an elf is a fairy creature
fans as a verb means stirs or kindles flames

explanation.surface: A tiny fairy rouses a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is to take or steal something, which is pinch in British slang.

clue.text: Perhaps Guinness works to eliminate boundaries?

indicators.note: eliminating boundaries removes the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: Is the Guinness brewery working to remove limits?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guinness' suggests the stout and its brewery works, but it is Sir Alec Guinness, the film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec Guinness was a famous British performer of stage and screen, an example of the category.

clue.text: Scratching head, expecting ruling

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: expecting is a euphemism for pregnant

explanation.surface: Puzzled about a pending decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as of a monarch currently in power.

clue.text: Oddly dismissing Carnegie Hall's backer and investor

indicators.note: dismissing the odd-numbered letters of Carnegie keeps only the even ones
a backer is at the back, so the final letter of Hall is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who funded Carnegie Hall, chosen by odd elimination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly dismissing' leaves ANGE from CARNEGIE; 'backer' also hints at the definition, as a theatrical backer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is someone who puts money into a venture, especially a stage production.

clue.text: Blush, stuck

definitions.meaning: to blush is to turn crimson in the face, read as two words
stuck here means pierced with horns, as by a bull

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means turn crimson; as one it means pierced by a horn.

clue.text: Vocal work of Mercury inspiring boy band at first

indicators.note: at first places the band ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a torc is an ancient neck band of twisted metal

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the symbol takes the boy inside it

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A song by Freddie Mercury that influenced a boy band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercury' points to Queen's singer Freddie, but it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch song is a sentimental ballad of unrequited love, a piece for the voice.

clue.text: Miniature bears puff and creep

indicators.note: bears means carries inside

parts.note: a toy dog is a miniature breed
a puff is a promotional ad

explanation.surface: Little teddies blow and crawl along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like teddy bears; it means holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a sycophantic flatterer, also called a creep.

clue.text: Unruly leaders of Viking hordes often cause absolute chaos

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the gathered letters are shuffled
leaders are the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Raiding Norse bands led by wild chiefs bring total disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' gives VHOCA, which 'Unruly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc means widespread destruction and disorder, synonymous with chaos.

clue.text: Radical change to sport's corporate image

parts.note: F1 is Formula One motor racing, with the figure 1 written as the letter I
a re-brand is a change of image, so the re- prefix supplies the change
a brand is a company's image

explanation.surface: A sweeping overhaul of a sport's branding.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads F1 REBRAND, a Formula One relaunch, with 1 standing as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a passionate agitator for change, so a radical in the noun sense.

clue.text: Behold Shakespearean heroine with retrograde moon

indicators.note: with signals the heroine's name carries the turned-round moon in place of its original

parts.note: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the moon's name is turned round

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Look at Viola alongside a moon going backwards in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' is an astronomers' word for a body moving backwards, apt for a moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila is a French-derived exclamation meaning there it is, like look or behold.

clue.text: Ageing yodeller dropping round, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
dropping means letting fall one letter of the word yodeller

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A yodeller getting old has sadly given up singing rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes O from YODELLER, leaving YDELLER to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes people who are getting old, an adjective like ageing.

clue.text: Scramble and vault on walls of Eton

indicators.note: on puts the second piece after the first
walls are the outside, so the first and last letters of Eton

parts.note: a crypt is an underground vault

explanation.surface: Clamber and leap over the walls of Eton College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' and 'vault' look like climbing verbs; Eton is the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt is to encode a message, the sense of scramble used for signals.
